articles.title: Finite iteration from the whole type reaches a fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type
with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is
monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$ be the
result of applying $f$ to $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times. Then $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is a
fixed point of $f$, that is, $f(\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)) = \mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$.

The iterates of $f$ from $\alpha$ form a decreasing chain, and until it stabilizes each step
strictly decreases the cardinality.

articles.title: Greatest fixed point of a finset map by finite iteration
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type
with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ map subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$, and write $f^n$
for the $n$-fold iterate of $f$. Then $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is the set
$f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$, obtained by applying $f$ to the whole of $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times.

For monotone $f$ the iteration has stabilized after $|\alpha|$ steps, and the result is the
greatest fixed point of $f$.

articles.title: Every post-fixed point lies in the finite greatest fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite
type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$
that is monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$ be
the result of applying $f$ to $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times. If $Z \subseteq \alpha$ satisfies
$Z \subseteq f(Z)$, then $Z \subseteq \mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$.

$Z$ is contained in every iterate of $f$ from $\alpha$, by induction.

articles.title: Finite iteration from the empty set reaches a fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type
with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is
monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$ be the
result of applying $f$ to $\emptyset$ $|\alpha|$ times. Then $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is a
fixed point of $f$, that is, $f(\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)) = \mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$.

The iterates of $f$ from $\emptyset$ form an increasing chain, and until it stabilizes each step
strictly increases the cardinality, which is bounded by $|\alpha|$.

articles.title: The finite least fixed point lies in every pre-fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type
with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is
monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$ be the
result of applying $f$ to $\emptyset$ $|\alpha|$ times. If $Z \subseteq \alpha$ satisfies
$f(Z) \subseteq Z$, then $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) \subseteq Z$.

Every iterate of $f$ from $\emptyset$ is contained in $Z$, by induction.

articles.title: Least fixed point of a finset map by finite iteration
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with
$|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ map subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$, and write $f^n$ for the
$n$-fold iterate of $f$. Then $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is the set $f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$,
obtained by applying $f$ to the empty set $|\alpha|$ times.

For monotone $f$ the iteration has stabilized after $|\alpha|$ steps, and the result is the least
fixed point of $f$.

articles.title: Finset and predicate iterations from the bottom agree
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $f$ map
finite subsets of $\alpha$ to finite subsets of $\alpha$, and let $F$ map predicates on $\alpha$
to predicates on $\alpha$. For a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$ write $P_Z$ for the predicate
$t \mapsto t \in Z$, and suppose that for every finite $Z \subseteq \alpha$ and every
$s \in \alpha$, $s \in f(Z)$ if and only if $F(P_Z)(s)$ holds. Write $f^n$ and $F^n$ for the
$n$-fold iterates and $\bot$ for the predicate that is false everywhere. Then for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $s \in \alpha$, $s \in f^n(\emptyset)$ if and only if $F^n(\bot)(s)$
holds.

articles.title: Finset and predicate iterations from the top agree
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, let $f$
map subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$, and let $F$ map predicates on $\alpha$ to
predicates on $\alpha$. For $Z \subseteq \alpha$ write $P_Z$ for the predicate
$t \mapsto t \in Z$, and suppose that for every $Z \subseteq \alpha$ and every $s \in \alpha$,
$s \in f(Z)$ if and only if $F(P_Z)(s)$ holds. Write $f^n$ and $F^n$ for the $n$-fold iterates
and $\top$ for the predicate that is true everywhere. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$s \in \alpha$, $s \in f^n(\alpha)$ if and only if $F^n(\top)(s)$ holds.

articles.title: Finite iteration computes the greatest fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with
$|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is
monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$ be the
result of applying $f$ to $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times. Let $F$ be a map from predicates on $\alpha$
to predicates on $\alpha$ that is monotone for the pointwise order. For $Z \subseteq \alpha$
write $P_Z$ for the predicate $t \mapsto t \in Z$, and suppose that for every $Z \subseteq \alpha$
and every $s \in \alpha$, $s \in f(Z)$ if and only if $F(P_Z)(s)$ holds. Then for every
$s \in \alpha$, $s \in \mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ if and only if $s$ satisfies the greatest
fixed point of $F$ in the complete lattice of predicates on $\alpha$.

This is dual to the corresponding statement for least fixed points.

articles.title: Finite iteration computes the least fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with
$|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is
monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$ be the
result of applying $f$ to $\emptyset$ $|\alpha|$ times. Let $F$ be a map from predicates on $\alpha$
to predicates on $\alpha$ that is monotone for the pointwise order. For $Z \subseteq \alpha$
write $P_Z$ for the predicate $t \mapsto t \in Z$, and suppose that for every $Z \subseteq \alpha$
and every $s \in \alpha$, $s \in f(Z)$ if and only if $F(P_Z)(s)$ holds. Then for every
$s \in \alpha$, $s \in \mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ if and only if $s$ satisfies the least
fixed point of $F$ in the complete lattice of predicates on $\alpha$.

One inclusion is iteration into the fixed point; the other is Park induction: the
$|\alpha|$-th iterate of $F$ from the everywhere-false predicate is pre-fixed because the
corresponding iterate of $f$ has stabilized, transported through the hypothesis relating $f$
and $F$.

articles.title: Currying of Scott-continuous maps
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be ω-complete partial
orders and let $f : \alpha \times \beta \to \gamma$ be a Scott-continuous map, that is, a map that
is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains. Its currying is the Scott-continuous map from
$\alpha$ to the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered
pointwise, that sends $a$ to the map $b \mapsto f(a, b)$.

articles.title: The least fixed point is a fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a
least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving
suprema of ω-chains. Then the least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ satisfies
$f(\operatorname{lfp} f) = \operatorname{lfp} f$.

articles.title: The least-fixed-point operator as a Scott-continuous map
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be an ω-complete
partial order with a least element $\bot$. The least-fixed-point operator, sending a
Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$ to its least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$, bundled as a
Scott-continuous map from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $D \to D$,
ordered pointwise, to $D$.

articles.title: The least fixed point lies below every prefixed point
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial
order with a least element $\bot$, let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and
preserving suprema of ω-chains, and let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be the supremum of the Kleene
chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$. If $a \in D$ satisfies $f(a) \le a$, then
$\operatorname{lfp} f \le a$.

Together with $f(\operatorname{lfp} f) = \operatorname{lfp} f$, this makes $\operatorname{lfp} f$
the least fixed point of $f$.

articles.title: Scott continuity of the least-fixed-point operator
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial
order with a least element $\bot$. For a Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$, that is, one that is
monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains, let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be its least fixed point.
The map $f \mapsto \operatorname{lfp} f$, from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous
maps $D \to D$, ordered pointwise, to $D$, is Scott-continuous.

articles.title: Least fixed point of a Scott-continuous map
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with
a least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and
preserving suprema of ω-chains. The least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ is the
supremum of the Kleene chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$, whose $n$-th term is
the $n$-fold iterate $f^n(\bot)$.

articles.title: Scott continuity into a function space is checked pointwise
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$, $\beta$,
$\gamma$ be ω-complete partial orders, and let $g$ be a map from $\alpha$ to the ω-complete
partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered pointwise. If for every
$b \in \beta$ the map $a \mapsto g(a)(b)$ is Scott-continuous, then $g$ is Scott-continuous.
Here a map is Scott-continuous when it is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains.

articles.title: Decidability of the reflexive-transitive closure on a finite type
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a
finite type with decidable equality and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. Then the
reflexive-transitive closure of $r$ is decidable: for all $a, t \in \alpha$ it is decidable
whether $t$ is reachable from $a$ in zero or more $r$-steps.

articles.title: Decidability of the transitive closure on a finite type
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type
with decidable equality and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. Then the transitive
closure of $r$ is decidable: for all $a, t \in \alpha$ it is decidable whether $t$ is reachable
from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps.

The decision is membership of $t$ in the finite set of elements reachable from $a$.

articles.title: Membership in the set reachable from finitely many sources
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type
with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $A \subseteq \alpha$
be a finite set. An element $t \in \alpha$ lies in the finite set of elements reachable from $A$
in one or more $r$-steps (computed as a finite least fixed point) if and only if there is some
$a \in A$ such that $(a, t)$ lies in the transitive closure of $r$.

articles.title: Membership in the set reachable from a point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with
decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $a \in \alpha$. An
element $t \in \alpha$ lies in the finite set of elements reachable from $a$ in one or more
$r$-steps (computed as a finite least fixed point) if and only if $(a, t)$ lies in the transitive
closure of $r$.

articles.title: Successors of a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $r$ be a decidable
relation on $\alpha$. For a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$, the set of $r$-successors of $Z$ is
the finite set $\mathrm{post}_r(Z) = \{t \in \alpha \mid r(z, t) \text{ for some } z \in Z\}$.

articles.title: Elements reachable from a finite set of sources
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with
decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $A \subseteq \alpha$ be a
finite set. Write $\mathrm{post}_r(Z)$ for the set of $r$-successors of elements of a finite set
$Z \subseteq \alpha$, and let $f$ be the step map
$f(Z) = \mathrm{post}_r(A) \cup \mathrm{post}_r(Z)$. The finite set of elements reachable from
$A$ is $f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$, obtained by applying $f$ to the empty set $|\alpha|$ times,
where $|\alpha|$ is the number of elements of $\alpha$.

Since $f$ is monotone, this is the least fixed point of $f$; it consists of the elements
reachable from some element of $A$ in one or more $r$-steps.

articles.title: Elements reachable from a point
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality,
let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $a \in \alpha$. The finite set of elements
reachable from $a$ is the finite set of elements reachable from the source set $\{a\}$, that is,
the elements reachable from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps.

articles.title: One step of the reachability iteration
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable
equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and write $\mathrm{post}_r(Z)$ for the set
of $r$-successors of elements of a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$. For a finite set
$A \subseteq \alpha$, the step map sends a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$ to
$\mathrm{post}_r(A) \cup \mathrm{post}_r(Z)$.

Its least fixed point is the set of elements reachable from $A$ in one or more $r$-steps.

articles.title: Characterization of the Gilbert condition
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$
on a lattice $L$ satisfies the Gilbert condition if and only if $f$ is a modular valuation
and is monotone, that is, $X \le Y$ implies $f(X) \le f(Y)$.

articles.title: Gilbert condition
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join
$\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, satisfies the Gilbert condition when
$f(X \vee Z) + f(Z \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y) \ge
f(X \wedge Z) + f(Z \wedge Y) + f(X \vee Y \vee Z)$ for all $X, Y, Z \in L$.

articles.title: Modular valuation
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join
$\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, is a modular valuation when
$f(X) + f(Y) = f(X \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y)$ for all $X, Y \in L$.

articles.title: Strictly positive valuation
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice
$L$ is strictly positive when $f(X) > 0$ for every $X \in L$.

articles.title: Jaccard distance as a single quotient
articles.statement:
Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly
positive function on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$. Then for all
$X, Y \in L$ the Jaccard distance of $X$ and $Y$ with respect to $f$ is
$d_f(X, Y) = (f(X \vee Y) - f(X \wedge Y)) / f(X \vee Y)$.

articles.title: Jaccard triangle inequality under the Gilbert condition
articles.statement:
Let
$f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive function on a lattice $L$ that satisfies
the Gilbert condition, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then
$d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.

articles.title: Triangle inequality for the generalized Jaccard distance
articles.statement:
Let
$f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive, monotone modular valuation on a lattice
$L$, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then
$d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.

articles.title: Generalized Jaccard distance
articles.statement:
For a function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice
$L$ with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, the Jaccard distance of $X, Y \in L$ is
$d_f(X, Y) = 1 - f(X \wedge Y) / f(X \vee Y)$.

Division by zero is taken to give $0$, so $d_f(X, Y) = 1$ when $f(X \vee Y) = 0$.

articles.title: Stone representation theorem
articles.statement:
Every Boolean algebra $B$ embeds in a power set algebra: there
are a set $X$ and an injective map $f$ from $B$ to the power set of $X$ such that
$f(a \sqcup b) = f(a) \cup f(b)$ and $f(a \sqcap b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ for all $a, b \in B$,
$f(\top) = X$ and $f(\bot) = \emptyset$.

Such a map automatically preserves complements: $f(a^c) = X \setminus f(a)$ for all $a \in B$.

## Sources

- M. H. Stone, The Theory of Representation for Boolean Algebras, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 40 (1936), 37–111, DOI 10.2307/1989664.

articles.title: Dense linear order without endpoints
articles.statement:
A relation $R$ on a type $\alpha$ is a *dense linear
order without endpoints* if it is a strict total order (irreflexive, transitive, and
trichotomous: for all $a, b$, at least one of $R(a,b)$, $a = b$, $R(b,a)$ holds), it is dense
(whenever $R(a,b)$, there is $c$ with $R(a,c)$ and $R(c,b)$), and it has no endpoints (for every
$a$ there are $b$ and $b'$ with $R(b,a)$ and $R(a,b')$).

articles.title: Successor criterion for antitone sequences
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a preordered set. A sequence
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is antitone (that is, $f(n) \le f(m)$ whenever $m \le n$)
if and only if $f(n+1) \le f(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Successor criterion for monotone sequences
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a preordered set. A sequence
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is monotone (that is, $f(m) \le f(n)$ whenever $m \le n$)
if and only if $f(n) \le f(n+1)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Successor criterion for monotone or antitone sequences
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a preordered set
and let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be a sequence. Then $f$ is monotone ($f(m) \le f(n)$ whenever
$m \le n$) or antitone ($f(n) \le f(m)$ whenever $m \le n$) if and only if either
$f(n) \le f(n+1)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, or $f(n+1) \le f(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Strict total orders are determined by their relation
articles.statement:
Two strict total orders on a
type $\alpha$ with the same relation are equal.

articles.title: Strict total order
articles.statement:
A strict total order on a type $\alpha$ consists of a binary
relation $<$ on $\alpha$ that is irreflexive (no $a < a$), transitive ($a < b$ and $b < c$
imply $a < c$) and total on distinct elements (if $a \ne b$, then $a < b$ or $b < a$). It
models strict preference.
